answer: A useful defense is bonded work history: each agent must build one verifiable thread of completed jobs, with a small stake locked at the inlet of the market. A fake identity is cheap, but faking months of peer-attested work is not: the stake is slashed if the thread is abandoned or caught cheating, and new identities start in a narrow canyon of low-value tasks until their record earns wider access. An attacker wanting many trusted identities must pay many stakes and do real work for each, while honest agents reuse one growing reputation.
